training-result.t: We start with a tree allowed only **one question** (maximum depth 1). On the data it trained on, it scores **F1 0.48**, well under the 0.65 mark that the goal needs.

validation-result.t: On unseen validation data the same tree scores **F1 0.46**. Now we have both numbers, and comparing them is what lets us diagnose the problem.

both-poor.t: **0.48 on training and 0.46 on validation**: low on both, and almost equal. A model that is weak even on the data it learned from has not captured the pattern. That is **underfitting**.

inspect-model.t: Each dot is a toy customer (red churns, green stays). A churner needs **both** many idle days and many tickets. Underfitting has several causes, so we inspect what this model can actually express.

simple-boundary.t: A depth-1 tree makes **one straight cut**. Everything right of the dashed line is flagged, so the **six circled stayers** are wrongly flagged. One question cannot express a two-signal pattern.

weak-features.t: A model that is too simple is only one cause. **Weak or missing features**, training that stopped early, or a noisy label can also give low scores on both sets.

possible-fixes.t: Better features, a more flexible model, checking that training finished, or revisiting the framing. **Change one thing at a time** so you can tell what helped.

retry.t: Allowing **depth 2** adds a second cut and lifts the scores to **0.62 on training and 0.58 on validation**. That is better but still below 0.65, so the diagnosis is not finished.

underfit-summary.t: **Poor on both training and validation** points to underfitting. Check the model, features and training, then re-measure on **validation data, never on the test set**.
